title: Keep owner, holder, site, supplier, status and restrictions separate
rationale: Owner, holder, site, supplier, status and restrictions answer different questions, so never infer one from another. A stock pool is the smallest amount that can be reserved on its own. Containers are optional detail. A partner count records when and how it was reported, how sure it is, and the evidence, and it never invents a reel or lot.

title: Reservations and minimum stock never move stock
rationale: A stock move changes the quantity, owner, holder, site or location. A reservation is a time-limited claim for one demand, and minimum stock is a standing amount to keep at a site, such as Keep local. Neither changes the quantity in stock. Work out what is available for each build after statuses, restrictions, other reservations and minimum stock; there is no single available total.

content: Show inventory simply and put exceptions first. Default to one compact, searchable table. Show local, partner, reserved or protected, in-transit or quarantined, and minimum-stock figures separately. Show 'available for this build' only when a specific demand is selected. A part's side sheet groups stock by site and holder, with containers, evidence and history one level deeper. Keep Receive, Move, Reserve and Keep local as the main actions. Each screen needs accessibility, screenshot and visual-review evidence at 1280x800.

name: Move stock between sites through one in-transit record
description: Record dispatch and receipt as separate facts that are safe to repeat, with one in-transit record between them. Count stock once, keep whole-piece quantities, and keep the owner, lot and reservation history. A partial transfer creates a separate, traceable child. When ordered stock arrives, Procurement stops counting it as inbound. Partner counts keep their source, date and confidence history, and never invent containers or lots.
